text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- A court hearing starts in Warsaw today to discover the assets of the co-ruling Social Democratic party (SdRP) of ex-communists. The party owes the state 20 million zlotys plus interest.
- Volkswagen Polo cars assembled in Poland go on sale next week. Their price has not yet been announced.

- The bankrupt Gdansk shipyard's receiver Andrzej Wiercinski said talks had begun with a major bank on financing five ships to be built for a German owner. He did not reveal the bank's name. The results of the talks should be known by the middle of next week.

- According to a report by the U.N. European Economic Commission in Geneva the value of direct foreign investment in former communist countries was $46 billion in mid-1996. The most, $13.9 billion, was invested in Hungary while Poland was in second place with 9.1 billion or 17 percent of the total.

- Within a month there should be a second invitation to buy shares in Browary Gornoslaskie brewery in Zabrze. This is the only brewery that has not been privatised and Poland's seventh largest in terms of output.
- At the turn of June and July this year the Krotoszyn council in Kalisz province aims to a non-public issue of municipal bonds worth five or six million zlotys.
- The company Big Carton aims to invest more than $300 million in two cardboard and paper factories over the next three years.

- The treasury ministry resumed the process of privatising the Zaklady Miesne meat plant in Ostroleka. There should soon be an invitation to initial talks on buying its shares, deputy minister Leszek Juchniewicz said.
- Meat processor Pekpol management forecasts that net revenue from sales this year will increase 25 percent and net profits will rise 35 percent compared with last year's results.
- The guarantors of a share issue by pharmaceutical company Jelfa SA, Bank Zachodni and CS First Boston, yesterday signed agreements on sub-guarantees for a total of 250,000 shares.
- At the turn of 1997 and 1998 there will probably be a public issue by the Morliny meat plant Zaklady Miesne Morliny.
